content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

I've drafted the baseline specification. **Per our Spec-Driven Development workflow, this is a review gate — nothing gets planned or built until you approve the spec.** Here it is for your review.

## Specification: Bookmark Manager

**Files created**
- `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md` — the specification
- `specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md` — quality checklist (all items pass)

### What the app does (in plain terms)

Three prioritized user journeys, each independently usable:

1. **Save a bookmark (P1)** — paste a URL, optionally a title/notes, and it's kept. Invalid URLs rejected; missing titles auto-derived. *This alone is a working product.*
2. **Browse & find (P2)** — see all bookmarks (newest first), search by keyword across title/address, open one in a new tab.
3. **Edit & delete (P3)** — fix a title/address/notes; delete with a confirmation step.

**Handled edge cases**: duplicate URLs, missing `http://`, unreachable pages, long titles, empty collection, no-search-matches.

**Measurable success targets**: save in <15s, find-in-100 via search in <5s, no data loss across restarts, responsive with 500+ bookmarks.

### Scope boundaries I assumed for v1 (please confirm)

These are the decisions most worth your attention — I chose reasonable defaults rather than blocking, but they define the scope:

| # | Decision | v1 default | Out of scope |
|---|----------|-----------|--------------|
| 1 | Users | Single user, **no login/accounts** | Multi-user, sharing |
| 2 | Platform | Browser-accessed **web app** | Native mobile |
| 3 | Organization | **Flat list + search** | Folders, tags |
| 4 | Storage | Single-instance local persistence | Cross-device sync, cloud backup |
| 5 | Entry | **Manual add only** | Browser/file import |

### Your options at this gate

- **Approve as-is** → I proceed to `speckit-plan` (the implementation plan gate).
- **Change something** → tell me what (e.g. "I want tags," "it needs user accounts," "add import"), and I'll revise the spec before planning.
- **Ambiguous / want to explore options** → I can run `speckit-clarify` to ask structured questions.

How would you like to proceed?

Please revise the specification before planning. The single-user web app with local storage is right, but the proposed flat, manual-only version leaves out important parts of how I want to manage a growing collection.

I need it to include:

- Tags on bookmarks, suggestions from existing tags while typing, and filtering by a tag.
- Automatic collection of the page title, description, icon, and preview image, while still letting me edit the title and description.
- Search across the address, title, description, notes, and tags. It should ignore letter case and support exact phrases, `#tag`, AND/OR/NOT, and grouped searches.
- Read-later status, with a separate unread view and a way to mark items read.
- Archiving as a reversible alternative to deletion, with archived items hidden from normal browsing and search and shown in their own view.
- Sorting options, rather than always forcing newest-first.
- Selecting multiple bookmarks—or everything matching the current search or filter—and applying actions such as tagging, marking read/unread, archiving, or deleting.
- Saved combinations of searches and included or excluded tags so I can return to those views.
- Notes that can contain formatting and display that formatting when viewed.
- A preserved local copy of the bookmarked page, including saving the original PDF when the link is a PDF, plus an option to preserve it through the Internet Archive.
- Importing and exporting standard browser bookmark files, preserving titles, tags, and original dates during import.
- Personal display choices such as default sorting, how many items are shown, and text size.

The duplicate behavior also needs to be more definite: saving the same address again should take me to the existing bookmark so I can edit it, never create another copy or silently replace information.

In the list, I expect to see the title, description, tags, and site icon, with selecting the bookmark taking me to the original page. Please update the specification with these behaviors and bring it back for approval.

### Key points worth your eye

- **List display (FR-033):** each row shows title, description, tags, and site icon; activating opens the original page.

- **Preservation is non-blocking (FR-029):** if a local copy, PDF grab, or Internet Archive submission fails, the bookmark still saves and the failure is surfaced.

All four corrections are in `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md` and back for your final review.

## What changed

1. **Editable address** — US1 scenario 2 and **FR-004** now cover editing address, title, description, tags, and note. Editing an address re-runs normalization + duplicate handling, so it can't create a duplicate.

2. **Bulk tag removal** — US7 scenario 3 and **FR-023** now list both *add tags* and *remove tags* among bulk actions.

3. **Search semantics** — two new requirements plus scenarios:
   - **FR-013a**: ordinary words and `#tag` combined without an operator → **implicit AND** (all must match); OR only where you write it.
   - **FR-013b**: `"AND"` / `"OR"` / `"NOT"` inside quotes are searched as **literal text**, not operators.

4. **Preservation format** — US9 scenarios, **FR-026/FR-027**, and the Preserved Copy entity: ordinary pages preserved as a **self-contained HTML file**; PDFs kept as the **original PDF** (never converted).

The quality checklist still passes with no open clarification markers.

## Implementation Plan: Bookmark Manager

**Artifacts generated** in `specs/001-bookmark-manager/`:
- `plan.md` — architecture & technical context
- `research.md` — 11 technical decisions (with rationale + rejected alternatives)
- `data-model.md` — entities, fields, indexes, visibility rules
- `contracts/api.md` — the HTTP/JSON API contract
- `quickstart.md` — run + validation guide mapping to every user story

### The proposed approach

**Stack** (all from the shared image, minimal footprint):
- **Node.js 24 + Express** — one process serving the JSON API *and* a build-free vanilla-JS browser client, bound to `0.0.0.0:4000` (matches the runtime environment; `npm start`).
- **SQLite via `better-sqlite3`** — local single-file DB; preserved page copies stored as files under `data/preserved/`.
- **Playwright 1.61.0 + shared Chromium** — metadata capture and self-contained HTML snapshots (pinned to the installed browser; no second download).
- **`cheerio`** (Netscape bookmark import/export), **`markdown-it` + `sanitize-html`** (formatted notes).

### How the trickier requirements are handled

| Requirement | Plan |
|---|---|
| **Duplicate → existing bookmark** | `normalized_url` is a **UNIQUE** column; repeat save/edit returns the existing bookmark (`duplicate:true` / 409), never a copy or silent overwrite |
| **Search semantics** | Hand-written tokenizer + recursive-descent parser → AST → parameterized SQLite. Encodes implicit-AND, quoted-operators-as-literal-text, precedence, `#tag`, phrases, case-insensitivity |
| **Preservation** | Content-type sniff: PDF → stream original `.pdf`; page → Chromium renders a single **self-contained HTML** file. All async/non-blocking |
| **Internet Archive** | Best-effort async "Save Page Now"; failures recorded and surfaced, never block save (and honestly reported if unreachable offline) |
| **Bulk actions** | `/api/bookmarks/bulk` supports add/remove tags, read/unread, archive, delete over an id-list *or* "all matching current query/filter" |
| **Performance (1,000+)** | DB-level filtering/sorting with indexes on archive/read/date/title and tag joins |

**Deliberately out of scope** (per approved spec): auth/multi-user, sync, native mobile, client build pipeline.

### At this gate

- **Approve** → I proceed to `speckit-tasks` (the actionable task breakdown), then pause again before implementing.
- **Adjust** → tell me what to change (e.g. a different storage choice, framework, or preservation format) and I'll revise the plan.

Shall I generate the task breakdown?
Yes, the plan supports the approved behavior and the failure handling sounds appropriate. Please proceed to the task breakdown and pause for review before implementation.

content:
The review server is live on `http://maker:4000` with a clean empty state. Both corrections are delivered and verified.

## Corrections delivered

Both are **fidelity fixes against the approved spec** — implementation only; spec, plan, and tasks unchanged.

### 1. "Select all matching" now spans the entire filter/search (FR-022)

- **Server** (`routes/bookmarks.js`): the bulk endpoint resolves a whole-result-set selector — `matchQuery`, `matchView`, `matchIncludedTags`/`matchExcludedTags`, or a saved-view id — via the DB, so actions apply to **every** matching bookmark, not just the loaded page.
- **Client** (`web/app.js`): checking "Select all" now reveals **"Select all N matching"**; clicking it switches the bulk bar to *"All N matching selected"*, and the action is sent as a filter selector rather than page ids. Selection resets when the filter/search/view changes.

### 2. A "successful" preserved page is now genuinely self-contained (FR-026/FR-029)

- **Server** (`services/preserve.js`): the snapshot now aggressively embeds stylesheets (including `@import` and their `url()` assets), images, and inline-style assets as data URIs, and strips external scripts/resource hints. It then **verifies** the result with a scanner (`findExternalResources`) and a server-side second pass for CORS-blocked assets.
- **Honest status**: if *any* external image/style/font reference remains, preservation is marked **`failed`** (no file presented) instead of `ready`. Only a truly self-contained file is reported as a successful `ready` copy. The card shows `local copy: failed` (in red) in that case.

## Verification (both cases)

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| **Unit + integration** (`npm test`) | ✅ **44/44** |
| **E2E** (`npm run test:e2e`) | ✅ **2/2** |

New coverage specifically for your two points:
- **Select-all-matching** — integration (`bulk.selectall.test.js`): with 30 bookmarks and page size 5, bulk archive/tag/mark via `matchTag` / `matchQuery` / `matchViewId` affects **all 30**, proving it reaches beyond the page. Plus an e2e (`selectall.spec.js`) that checks the *"Select all 12 matching"* escalation and archives all 12 across pages.
- **Self-contained preservation** — unit (`preserve.scan.test.js`) for the verifier, and a deterministic integration test (`preserve.fail.test.js`): a page with an **unreachable external image is marked `failed` with no stored file**, while a fully self-contained page is `ready`. I also live-verified that a real rich page (playwright.dev) embeds to **0 external references**.

The app is running clean and empty for your acceptance review. If anything else needs adjustment, I'll route it through the same method (fidelity fix vs. spec change).

Note on the runtime: `pgrep`/`pkill` aren't available in this shell, which left stale detached servers around during testing (the noise you may have seen); I cleaned them up by PID via `/proc`, and pinned e2e to a dedicated port with a single worker so the suite is now stable.
Both corrections now match the approved behavior, and the verification covers the important edge cases. I accept the completed application.
